subject: Surge safeguard proposal — tiered adjudication & discount ladder
messages:
From: Clare Donovan <clare.donovan@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary surge coverage for launch week

Hi Rachel —

We have a hard launch scheduled for Apr 12 and our preliminary load tests show a likely 3x spike in token consumption for a 72-hour window. Procurement asked me to check whether Redwood can provide a short runway (safety net) to avoid throttles or emergency overrun invoices for that period.

Specific asks:
- A temporary quota uplift or a burst buffer for launch week (Apr 12–14)
- Clear, capped overrun rates if we exceed the buffer (so our finance team can model worst-case)
- One-off promotional discount consideration for the first month of production

We’re willing to sign a one-page mutual action plan or incorporate an addendum to our existing MSA. Can you outline options and a one-line summary for our procurement?

Thanks —
Clare
Clare Donovan
Head of Platform Ops, Clearline Health
clare.donovan@clearlinehealth.com
(415) 555-0142

---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Clare Donovan <clare.donovan@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary surge coverage for launch week

Hi Clare — thanks for the heads-up, and congrats on the launch progress. We can absolutely cover that window with a pragmatic safety-net approach that balances predictability for you and operational guardrails for us. High-level proposal below; attaching a detailed rate ladder so procurement has numbers.

High-level proposal (summary line for procurement): Temporary burst buffer equivalent to 200k tokens/day for Apr 12–14 with a tiered overrun ladder (discounted first tier, then blended overrun pricing) and a simple one-page addendum to the MSA.

Operational details:
- Burst buffer: 600k tokens total across the 72‑hour window (200k tokens/day).
- Overrun adjudication ladder:
  * Tier A (first 200k excess tokens across window): 30% discount off list overrun rate
  * Tier B (next 300k): 10% discount off list
  * Tier C (beyond 500k): standard overrun rate (no discount)
- Billing: Overrun consumption will be true‑up in the following month’s invoice with a line item referencing the addendum.
- Acceptance criteria: Clearline confirms anticipated peak day and agrees to share a brief post‑launch spike report (token consumption by route) for fairness reconciliation.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement: one-line summary + attach proposed-rate-ladder.xlsx (attached)
2) Redwood: we’ll draft a one‑page addendum (MA excerpt) and share for sign-off
3) If you want an extra concession for the first invoice we can propose a one‑time promotional credit (to be approved by finance) — payload depends on volume.

Attachment: proposed-rate-ladder.xlsx (breaks down per-token pricing by tier and example invoices)

Would Ben / Karthik like to weigh in on the commercial/legal constraints?

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 6 Mar 2027 14:30:00 -07:00

Forwarding my notes for clarity / legal.

On Thu, Mar 4, 2027 at 11:05 AM Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Clare — thanks for the heads-up, and congrats on the launch progress. We can absolutely cover that window with a pragmatic safety-net approach that balances predictability for you and operational guardrails for us. >
> High-level proposal (summary line for procurement): Temporary burst buffer equivalent to 200k tokens/day for Apr 12–14 with a tiered overrun ladder (discounted first tier, then blended overrun pricing) and a simple one-page addendum to the MSA.

Ben's notes:
- Finance preference: express the discount as a fixed $/k token equivalent in the spreadsheet so AP can model (I flagged that in the attachment).
- Credit authority: Sales can offer up to 35% credit on the first 200k tokens (needs RevOps OK). 30% is safe but we can stretch to 35% for strategic deals.
- Legal: prefer a short addendum that calls the window an "Ephemeral Burst" and ties reconciliation to the monthly consumption report. Avoid language that creates a continuing commitment to uplift beyond the specified window.
- Procurement ask: provide a single-line summary and a DocuSign-ready addendum excerpt (MA-draft-excerpt.pdf attached).

Suggested counters:
- Keep Rachel's tier amounts but change Tier A discount to 35% as a one-time concession if we get a signed addendum + PO before Mar 22.
- Include a cap on total discounted spend (e.g., max promotional credit $X) — makes finance comfortable.

I can approve the 35% concession if RevOps signs off; looping Karthik for capacity/ops confirmation and to sanity-check runbook for the window.

Attachment: MA-draft-excerpt.pdf (one-page addendum template)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Rachel / Ben —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the two attachments. Procurement asked for a one-line summary (we’ll paste into the PO) and a DocuSign-ready addendum so we can turn quickly.

One-line (procurement-ready): Redwood to provide a 72-hour Ephemeral Burst of 600k tokens (200k/day) for Apr 12–14; Tiered overrun pricing with 35% promotional credit on the first 200k overrun if PO and signed addendum received by Mar 22; capped promotional credit of $12,000.

A few clarifying asks before we sign:
- Can you confirm the exact list overrun $/k token so AP can budget? (If you include a small worked example invoice row that would help.)
- We would like the addendum to call out the reconciliation deliverable (post-launch consumption report) due within 10 business days.
- Is Redwood able to provide a DocuSign link for the addendum?

We’re fine with the 35% concession with the $12k cap. If you could send the DocuSign + the one-page addendum (with the example invoice row) I’ll route immediately to AP.

Appreciate the speed — this launch has a hard date and we don’t have flexibility on our end.

Best,
Clare
